What the Mac app needs

HardwareApple silicon Mac. Intel release not available.
macOSBuild target: macOS 14+. Testing so far used macOS 27.0.1; the minimum supported release is not yet established.
App accessAccessibility permission, only for correcting inside apps you enable.
Optional contextRequires a compatible on-device model on macOS 26 or later. Basic correction does not require AI.
iPhone / iPadBrowser preview only. No native iOS keyboard has been released.

Current status

Version 0.18.0 is an open-source development preview. The Mac app has automated coverage for keyboard recovery, Unicode-safe editing and Undo. It now leaves skipped bulk input alone on later keystrokes. The website has separate Chrome and Safari checks for correction and standard Undo/Redo. Web checks do not establish native Mac compatibility.

Everyday physical typing, real IME switching, fresh installation on another Mac, older macOS versions, VoiceOver and the final signed installer remain release gates. The source is available for developers; the general Mac download stays closed.

View source on GitHub →

Once the verified download is available

  1. Download and unzip idkthen. Move it to Applications, then open it.
  2. Find idkthen in the menu bar. Choose English plus up to three other languages.
  3. Try a correction and Undo in Getting Started before granting app access.
  4. Allow Accessibility in System Settings → Privacy & Security. Reopen idkthen if needed.
  5. Add one app, turn on While You Type, and test in a multiline text field. Start with Suggest if you want to review every change.

If macOS reports an unidentified developer or cannot verify this download, stop and check the release. We do not recommend disabling Gatekeeper or removing quarantine.

Updates that you control

This preview does not install updates automatically. A future verified release will appear on this page with its version and SHA-256 checksum. Quit idkthen before replacing the app, keep it in Applications, and check Accessibility after reopening.
